title: Give every steward-channel request an Acceptance section and Files line
summary: Add one shared steward-request builder (in steward.rs) that always emits an `Acceptance:` section of `- ` bullets and a `Files:` line in the format `athena plan` parses. Route the structural-pass, design-review and introspection follow-up writers through it. Make the structural-pass dedupe ignore closed passes. The audience is the drain/plan loop, which today refuses 30 Athena-written requests.

defaults_applied.how: New tests for each writer, the structural-pass bullets and the reopen-after-close dedupe; fmt, clippy and test criterion.
The fix is at the writers via a shared builder, not in the parser.
Criteria run the writers' output through the real parse and check the hook queues again after close.
Behavior criteria name cargo test, clippy and fmt --check.
The shared builder enforces the format, and a test covers every writer.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Goal: every request Athena writes for itself is schedulable by `athena plan`. The audience is the drain loop and the person reading its refusals.
The parse `athena plan` uses for request-text acceptance lives mainly in reading.rs and plan.rs. The test calls it directly, and reading.rs changes only if a small exported helper is needed.

The introspection follow-up writer builds its text through ProposedChange.request, applied by RequestQueue in steward.rs, with text composed in introspect.rs. The shared builder goes in steward.rs and callers in introspect.rs and code_health.rs use it.
Closing the old refused passes is an operational step by the user, not part of the change.
Per the 'Fix the root cause at the writers, not the parser' instruction, the plan parser's behavior is not loosened.

acceptance_criteria.text: A test builds the text from each steward-channel writer (structural pass, design review, introspection follow-up, and any other writer found building a steward request) and runs it through the same acceptance and files parse that `athena plan` uses. None is refused for missing acceptance and each yields a non-empty file list. Run `cargo test`.

A test builds a structural-pass request for a fixture file over each limit. The text has an `Acceptance:` section whose `- ` bullets name the breached limits as measured (lines, function length, weekly landings). The bullets also say no behavior change with existing tests passing, and that fmt, clippy and test pass. The text has a `Files:` line naming the file. Run `cargo test`.
A test queues a structural pass for a file over its limits and closes that job. The next hook run (`code_health_after_landing`) queues a new structural pass for the same file. Run `cargo test`.

A single shared builder for steward requests exists, and every steward-channel writer constructs its text through it. A writer cannot omit `Acceptance:` bullets or `Files:`. The code or tests make this enforced rather than relying on convention.
Closed, including refused, earlier structural passes count as not open in the dedupe. A still-open pass for the same file still suppresses a duplicate, and the existing test for that keeps passing.
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` all pass.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing the steward request format fix and the dedupe change.

out_of_scope: Changing the plan parser to accept requests that lack acceptance
Restructuring the files that the passes name, such as run.rs
The introspection follow-up job contents (reading-input and no-change guard)
departures: The change spans several writers plus a new shared builder and tests across three or four files, so cost and time are somewhat above the reference median.
urgent_reason: Every refused steward request is a wasted queued job whose lesson never runs, so fixing the writers cuts that failed, redo-prone work.
